newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk navy ships leave to visit Turkish Cypriot port.
newsitem.headline: Turk navy ships leave to visit Turkish Cypriot port.

text.p: Three Turkish navy ships left for northern Cyprus on Friday in a show of solidarity with the breakaway Turkish Cypriot state, a military official said.
"A frigate and two assault boats are on the way to Cyprus since this morning," the official told Reuters.

Turkey has promised closer military and political links with the self-declared Turkish Cypriot republic in response to Greek Cypriot plans to install anti-aircraft missiles from Russia in the south of the island.
The ships are due to arrive at the port of Famagusta on the eastern coast of Turkish Cyprus on Saturday at 9.00 a.m. local time (0700 GMT), the offical said.
"It is planned they will stay there for four days," he said. According to state-run Anatolian news agency the vessels will be open to visits by Turkish Cypriots during that time.

Ankara, which has 30,000 soldiers stationed on Cyprus, has threatened a military strike against the S-300 missiles if Greek Cyprus goes ahead with their deployment. They are not expected to be installed within the next 16 months.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a Greek Cypriot coup backed by Athens.
